steps.description: Give the Bamboo Slip to Gendou
Wait for the impostor Gendou at night (21:00 – 23:00)
Wait for the fake Gendou to show up
Use Elemental Sight to pursue the fake Gendou
Obtain a set of Lyudochka's clothes
Report back to Momoyo and talk to her
Ask Momoyo to start making the fake cadaver
Hand over the set of Lyudochka's clothes

dialogs.content: #{NICKNAME}, look! There's someone walking out from the shrine!
That's our mark, alright! The fake Gendou! She's heading down the mountain. C'mon, after her!
It hasn't come time yet to meet the Teacher, I'm sure of it. In that case, this must be about that incident...
Lyudochka.
Ah, Teacher, you're here!
Sorry for bothering you. Allow me to make my report. So, concerning your instructions to infiltrate the Shuumatsuban...
Enough, Lyudochka. I tire of your delaying tactics.
"Frequent contact might raise suspicion," "The Shuumatsuban's direction may change due to the end of the Vision Hunt Decree, I must gather more information"...
You always say these things! Tell me. You don't actually have the trust of those two Shuumatsuban members, do you? Why else would you spout all these lies, hoping to stave me off?
That's not it, Teacher! They do trust me. I just need a little more time...
Time, you say? I have given you more than sufficient time.
Understand this. My patience is limited, as is that of Lady Arlecchino.
My apologies...
I did not spend all those years raising you to listen to apologies. What I want are results. Results!
...Forget it. I will not chase down every little detail of this matter. Your inability to win their trust, your present lifestyle getting to your head... None of this matters.
I have written your "final instructions" on this sheet of paper. Take it, and read it well.
Yes, Teacher! I will complete the mission. I will not disappoint you!
...Th—This is!?
Is something wrong?
Ah, no. Not at all...
Lyudochka. May I take your previous words as your promise?
Answer me. Yes? Or no?
Teacher! I have no objections to your decision. But... You said that Lady Arlecchino can recall us from Inazuma at any time.
And at this moment, the Shogunate and Watatsumi Island have reached a ceasefire, so... Is what we're doing really necessary?
Hah. That is precisely why our mission has value.
Lady Signora may have met her end here in Inazuma, but that makes it the best time for us to repay Lady Arlecchino's kindness and build up her prestige.
And I have always told you that as far as we are concerned, "chaos" is the most fertile soil.
What are you wavering for, Lyudochka?
This way, there will certainly be more orphans...
And wouldn't that be well? We can take them in and train them. They will join us — well, provided you complete your mission, of course.
Do not disappoint me again, Lyudochka. We go many years back. I have no wish to take things too far.
Ohh...
Oh no, something terrible's going to happen to Watatsumi Island!
#Looks like Lyudochka's alone now, {NICKNAME}. Let's find a way to get those final instructions from her!
Lyudochka.
Who's there!?
#You... {NICKNAME}, why are you here?
That, I... No, you misunderstand! I... I was here because...
I don't think I'm misunderstanding anything.
You responded when I called you "Lyudochka."
...Well, well, I suppose there's no point saying anything now.
Now that you've exposed my true identity, I can't let you leave alive!
Your clothes say it all.
*cough* Ugh... *pants*
Hey, are you alright?
Sorry. I didn't quite hold back enough.
*pants* Why... aren't you finishing me off?
You must be trying to get those final instructions from me. Well? Wouldn't it be simpler to just be rid of me first?
That would certainly be simple, yes.
I suppose that might even be a release for you.
Gendou... No, Ms. Lyudochka. We can tell, y'know? You came at us pretty hard at first, but you weren't serious at all while the two of you were fighting, were you?
Your attacks were pretty fake, too.
Eh? I... I wasn't faking it that much, was I?
Well, you were certainly trying to finish things — for yourself, at least.
Ms. Lyudochka, we overheard your conversation with that Teacher of yours. Things... seem kinda tough. Could you tell us what happened? We can help you!
But I... I'm a Fatuus.
Paimon said we would help — and so we will.
#Aw, thanks, {NICKNAME}!
That's right! Don't you worry, we don't hurt good people!
I... I wouldn't call myself a good person.
At first, I only infiltrated the Grand Narukami Shrine so that I could make contact with members of the Shuumatsuban and infiltrate their ranks in turn.
But imagine my surprise when I found out that the two Shuumatsuban members the Teacher spoke of were, in fact, the Traveler — famed for their deeds in Mondstadt and Liyue — and their servitor.
Paimon's not a... servitor, or whatever!
No wonder you knew my name.
Correct. As such, I knew that the Shuumatsuban infiltration was a bust from the start.
But the Teacher had such great expectations for this operation, so I didn't know how to report this to him. If he knew the truth, his wrath would be... That wouldn't have ended well for me.
And yet, coming to Inazuma, becoming a shrine maiden... It was all like a dream! And I would have been satisfied just being able to dream this dream.
So I kept finding reasons to procrastinate and prevaricate, trying to take everything one day at a time.
I thought that my lies would fall through one day. I certainly never expected the Teacher to not pursue the matter, but give me a new mission instead.
What mission did he give you, anyway? You went pale as a sheet the moment you read that note!
That's because my mission... is "to poison."
P—Poison!?

The Teacher has ordered me and several others to enter Watatsumi Island and poison the land, before intentionally exposing our respective identities as a shrine maiden at the Grand Narukami Shrine and soldiers of the Tenryou Commission.
That way, we would stir up conflict between the Shogunate and Watatsumi Island, which would give us, the Fatui, a chance to enter the equation.
That "Teacher" of yours... What a wicked person! If that plan went through, all the work people have put in to re-establish peace in Inazuma would go right down the drain!
So what do you plan to do, Lyudochka?
I... I don't know. I don't have the right to oppose the Teacher's orders, but I don't want to see such a thing happen!
That's because you're a "Snezhevna," right?
#Come to think of it, Paimon's heard that word used a lot. What does that mean? You already seem to know, {NICKNAME}!
It's used to refer to orphans, isn't it?
That's correct. "Snezhevich" and "Snezhevna" are surnames the Fatui give to orphans they take in, like us.
We grew up in an orphanage set up by Lady Arlecchino. We do not know who we truly are. At the most, we know the blood that flows through our veins.
It was due to my Inazuman heritage that I studied matters concerning this land since I was young.
In fact, my Teacher is also a Snezhevich. That's why I can't understand... No. That's why I cannot forgive him for saying those things.
I've always been thinking to myself: who am I, really? Why was I left all alone? Did my parents meet with some unfortunate fate? Or did they abandon me?
But the way the Teacher completely disregarded the suffering of orphans... I couldn't help but wonder: was my fate a creation of the Fatui? Of people like the Teacher?
Truly unforgivable.
#{NICKNAME}, we've gotta help Ms. Lyudochka. She might be with the Fatui, but she isn't a bad person.
Thank you for your sentiments, but I suspect that my course is already set. The Teacher will have no mercy on traitors. As long as I live, he will find me.
Perhaps meeting my fate at your hands might have been best.
Is that the only way you can get away from him? That can't be!
Huh. Wait. Paimon's remembering something...
Momoyo, yes?
Momoyo? Right! Paimon's got it now. She was making some cad—
Hush.
Ahem! *cough* So basically, Ms. Lyudochka, we've come up with a way to save you — and foil your Teacher's awful plot in the process!
Huh? Really?
Don't you worry about a thing! Still, you'd best find a place to lie low for the next few days. You can come out once we're done settling everything.
Do you know of any place to go? Someplace we can find you but that no one will suspect might be best!
Let me think...
Ah, there is one place. I once worked at Yae Publishing House as a proofreader for new novel releases under a pseudonym. I... really loved their novels.
They have a small room behind their bookstore in Inazuma City, which is sometimes used by proofreaders — or authors behind on their manuscript submissions.
That sounds like a fine spot!
Talk about "hidden in plain sight."
Ms. Lyudochka, just hide out in that spot for a bit. We'll come looking for you if anything crops up.
I understand. I... really don't know how I should thank you. I mean, I've been deceiving you all this time...
The Teacher wrote the details of our mission on the piece of paper he gave me. Here. The lives of the innocents of Watatsumi Island are in your hands now.
Lyudochka departs.
She's gone. We'd best head back to see Momoyo. Looks like we've still got quite a few important things to get done.
No wonder you knew about us.
Well, if you really are in trouble here...
Your laughter was plenty fake, too.
You're only back now? Well then. Did you get the intel?
You're back.
The crafting will take a whole day, so come back tomorrow. Stop floating around me, you'll ruin my mood.
I'll continue to work as a proofreader here for now. I pray for your success.
How's the proofreading going, by the way?
It's going quite smoothly, but there's a lot of content to go through. And considering that Yae Publishing House will be short-handed for the next two days... It'll be a long night, I think.
That sounds tough!
Haha. It is, but I find it fascinating! Being able to read the novels I love in advance, and even touch the hand-written manuscripts themselves... Ah, it's so wonderful!
Go on, quickly now. Get the powder onto that fake, and we'll be able to track her using Elemental Sight.
The Fatui are surely up to no good on Watatsumi Island. But now that the Tenryou Commission isn't covering for them, they can forget about trying anything funny.
Ah, an outlander! Hello!
Did you see anything earlier?
Oh yeah, I did.
I saw a shrine maiden lady walk over there... and then turn all purple, like, fwoosh! Then she flew away! That was super cool!
Ms. Lyudochka, are you there?
#Ah, it's {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Did something not go as planned? Don't worry, I'll leave this place immediately. I won't trouble you any further...
No, no! We came here because our current plan requires a set of your clothes — we'll need a set with which people can identify you immediately.
A highly-identifiable set of clothes? Alright.
This is my Fatui uniform. Those who know me should be able to recognize this set in particular.
Feels kinda warm to the touch.
Ah, I apologize, but I was wearing it under my other clothes in case of an emergency.
Alright. Now that we have this set of clothes, this plan should go off without a hitch!
Thank you, and best of luck.
Not bad. With this, we should be able to foil the Fatui's scheme. I will get people to perform follow-up operations immediately. You need no longer worry.
Actually, Momoyo, we've got something to ask of you...
You tell Momoyo the details of what happened.
Uhh, Momoyo, stop staring at Paimon. Um... Just say something, would you?
You want to save a Fatuus? What has that got to do with me!?
That woman replaced me, you know? If it wasn't for your overly fortuitous bumbling, the Shuumatsuban might be in a crisis right now!
#Um, {NICKNAME}, help Paimon out here! If we can't convince Momoyo, Ms. Lyudochka's life might be in danger!
Make a pitiful puppy-dog expression.
Hmph. That won't work on me. I will not associate with these Fatui!
Do you two think that making cadavers is so simple? I've been working day and night this whole time you've been out fishing for intel to finish the work I currently had.

You need this much <color=#00E1FFFF>Raw Meat</color> to constitute one person's weight! And then you also need to smelt <color=#00E1FFFF>White Iron Chunks</color> together with a plethora of other ingredients to make fake bones!
And without any <color=#00E1FFFF>Sea Ganoderma</color>, the body will not contain sufficient fat. It won't look convincing at all.
And putting the <color=#00E1FFFF>clothes</color> on the fake cadaver is just the worst when you need to create any realistic burns. Go too far, and those clothes will be all but unrecognizable!

What? Did you both go deaf? What are you standing around for? <color=#00E1FFFF>Eight hunks of Raw Meat, four White Iron Chunks, and three Sea Ganoderma</color>, plus one set of clearly identifiable <color=#00E1FFFF>clothes</color>!
We knew you were a great person, Momoyo!
Ugh, just scram! Quit bugging me already!
Make your best pitiful puppy-dog expression.
Make your best pitiful puppy-dog expression, plus imminent tears.
Alright, everything's ready. What happens after this is none of your business.
What about the operation that's happening on Watatsumi Island?
I had it arranged while you were out looking for these materials.
The item you need will take a whole day to craft, so come back tomorrow.
When that time comes, we will talk about how we might use this dummy body.
So, do you have some clothes with which people can easily identify Lyudochka?

The materials are <color=#00E1FFFF>eight hunks of Raw Meat</color>, <color=#00E1FFFF>four White Iron Chunks</color>, and <color=#00E1FFFF>three Sea Ganoderma</color>. Plus one set of <color=#00E1FFFF>clothes</color> with which to distinguish Lyudochka.
If you've got it, get going! I still need to arrange the operation to capture the Fatui on Watatsumi Island.
Hmph. When did I say that I wanted these materials?
But now that you've laid them out in front of me, I suppose I can help you. Your intelligence will save many lives, after all.
Raw Meat, White Iron Chunks, Sea Ganoderma... These will do.
